Front: A loop invariant must hold when?
Back: Before each iteration — Initialization and preservation make it available at termination.

Front: T(n)=T(n-1)+1 has tight growth?
Back: Theta(n) — There are n successive constant-work levels.

Front: Two consecutive n-iteration loops cost?
Back: Theta(n) — Their counts add to 2n.

Front: A loop doubles i from 1 while i<n. Its growth is?
Back: Theta(log n) — After k iterations i is 2^k.

Front: O(n) is a statement about what?
Back: An upper growth bound — Big-O does not itself specify which input case is being analysed.

Front: A stack removes which item?
Back: Most recently pushed — LIFO removes the top.

Front: A queue removes which item?
Back: Oldest enqueued — FIFO preserves arrival order.

Front: The efficient Python queue operation is?
Back: deque.popleft() — Deque removal from the left is constant-time.

Front: Circular queue: capacity5, head4, size 2. Next insertion index?
Postfix 9 4 - 2 * evaluates to?
Back: 10 — Compute9-4 first, then multiply by 2.

Front: Random access to the kth singly linked node takes?
Back: O(k) traversals — Follow next pointers from the head.

Front: Prepending to a singly linked list takes?
Back: O(1) — Change new.next and head.

Front: Appending with a maintained tail takes?
Back: O(1) — The tail identifies the attachment point.

Front: Deleting a known doubly linked node generally needs?
Back: Constant link updates — Its predecessor and successor are directly available.

Front: During reversal, prev denotes?
Back: The reversed processed prefix — Current points at the untouched suffix.

Front: A hash collision means?
Back: Two keys map to one bucket — Unequal keys may share a hash or bucket.

Front: For n=15,m=10, load factor is?
Back: 1.5 — Alpha=n/m.

Front: Can separate chaining have alpha>1?
Back: Yes — Buckets can each contain multiple entries.

Front: Linear probing mainly suffers from?
Back: Primary clustering — Contiguous runs attract more collisions.

Front: Deleting an open-address entry should usually leave?
Back: A tombstone — Search must continue through the old collision chain.

Front: Linear search requires sorted input?
Back: No — It can inspect arbitrary sequences.

Front: With a uniform successful position among n items, expected linear-search comparisons are?
Back: (n+1)/2 — Average the counts1 through n.

Front: Binary search needs which combination for logarithmic running time?
Back: Sorted order and efficient midpoint access — Both elimination and access assumptions matter.

Front: Inclusive binary-search loop condition is?
Back: lo<=hi — A single remaining candidate must still be examined.

Front: For n=15, maximum midpoint probes in standard binary search is?
Back: 4 — floor(log2 15)+1=4.

Front: Standard selection sort makes how many key comparisons on n items?
Back: n(n-1)/2 — Suffix lengths are n-1,n-2,...,1.

Front: Standard selection sort is generally?
Back: Unstable — Distant swaps can reverse equal keys.

Front: One left-to-right bubble pass fixes what?
Back: A maximum at the right end — The largest encountered value bubbles right.

Front: Early-stop bubble best-case time is?
Back: Theta(n) — One no-swap pass verifies sorted order.

Front: Insertion sort’s processed prefix is?
Back: Sorted but not necessarily globally smallest — Later keys can be smaller than every processed one.

Front: Merging sorted lengths p and q takes?
Back: O(p+q) — Each pointer advances at most its run length.

Front: Standard merge sort worst-case time is?
Back: Theta(n log n) — Balanced levels each perform linear merging work.

Front: Stable merging resolves equal keys by choosing?
Back: The earlier left-run record — That preserves original equal-key order.

Front: Lomuto partition puts the pivot where?
Back: At a valid final sorted position — Its rank determines the split, not a balance guarantee.

Front: Endpoint-pivot quicksort on sorted distinct data can take?
Back: Theta(n^2) — Each split can have sizes0 and n-1.

Front: Leaf height under the edge-count convention is?
Back: 0 — The longest downward path has zero edges.

Front: A perfect binary tree of height3 has nodes?
A full binary tree with 7 internal nodes has leaves?
Back: 8 — Leaves=internal nodes+1.

Front: Inorder traversal of a distinct-key BST yields?
Back: Sorted keys — The left-root-right property applies recursively.

Front: Preorder begins with?
Back: The root — Preorder visits root before subtrees.

Front: In a min-heap, the root is?
Back: A minimum — Parent order holds along every path.

Front: Zero-based children of index i are?
Back: 2i+1 and 2i+2 — These are the complete-tree array positions.

Front: Heap insertion needs at most?
Back: O(log n) sift-up work — The new item can travel one root-to-leaf path.

Front: Extract-min first replaces the root with?
Back: The last leaf — This preserves complete-tree shape before sift-down.

Front: Bottom-up heapify is?
Back: Theta(n) — Most nodes have small subtree height.

Front: An undirected simple graph with 5 vertices has at most edges?
Back: 10 — Choose an unordered pair of distinct vertices.

Front: Sum of undirected degrees equals?
Back: 2E — Every edge contributes two endpoints.

Front: Total directed indegree equals?
Back: E — Each directed edge has one head.

Front: Adjacency-list space is?
Back: O(V+E) — Store vertices plus their incident/outgoing entries.

Front: Matrix edge lookup takes?
Back: O(1) — Access the cell for the vertex pair.

Front: BFS uses which frontier?
Back: Queue — FIFO exploration produces distance layers.

Front: DFS recursion implicitly uses?
Back: A stack — Active calls retain the return path.

Front: BFS distances are shortest when edges have?
Back: Equal positive weight or unit cost — Ordinary BFS minimises number of edges.

Front: With adjacency lists, full BFS/DFS time is?
Back: O(V+E) — Each vertex and edge is handled a bounded number of times.

Front: For directed DFS, a grey-neighbour edge is?
Back: A cycle witness — It reaches an active ancestor.

Front: Relaxation replaces d[v] when?
Back: d[u]+w<d[v] — Only a cheaper discovered route improves the bound.

Front: Dijkstra settles the vertex with?
Back: Smallest tentative total distance — The global frontier minimum is the greedy choice.

Front: Dijkstra permits zero-weight edges?
Back: Yes — Its assumption is nonnegative, not strictly positive.

Front: Bellman–Ford uses at most ordinary passes?
Back: V-1 — A simple shortest path has at most V-1 edges.

Front: An improvement on an extra Bellman–Ford pass indicates?
Back: A reachable negative cycle — No simple finite optimal path can need more than V-1 edges.

Front: A greedy choice needs what to establish correctness?
Back: A proof such as exchange or cut reasoning — Local attractiveness alone is insufficient.

Front: For coins1,3,4 and target6, the minimum count is?
Back: 2 — 3+3 beats greedy4+1+1.

Front: Kruskal processes edges by?
Back: Increasing weight — It repeatedly considers a lightest remaining candidate.

Front: Disjoint-set union answers whether vertices are?
Back: In the same current component — It tracks partition membership.

Front: Path compression changes what?
Back: Parent pointers toward representatives — It accelerates later find operations.
